# ruststream-sqlx

> `ruststream-sqlx` brings SQL databases into RustStream, a Rust framework for services that subscribe to message brokers and publish to them, through `sqlx`: task queues in the service's own Postgres, MySQL/MariaDB and SQLite tables, served as a RustStream broker, and a transactional outbox over any RustStream broker.

A queue table is described by a struct: `#[derive(Inbox)]` with `#[inbox(..)]` and `#[field(..)]` roles, or `InboxTable` with the typed builder `InboxSpec` by hand. `SqlxBroker::from_url(url, pool_options)` serves the tables of the service's database through a pool it builds when the service starts (`SqlxBroker::new(pool)` takes a pool the service shares), `InboxQueue::<Row>::new("name")` is a subscription, and a table takes its rows by row lock, by lease or by advisory lock. The outbox is `#[derive(Outbox)]`, `outbox!` and two middlewares. A service imports `ruststream_sqlx::prelude::*`, and tests run the production app on `TestApp::start` over a real database, SQLite in memory needing no server.

This site holds the guides, one page per component and the architecture of the crate; the API reference is on docs.rs, and the framework itself is documented on the RustStream site.

## Guides

- [Guides](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-sqlx/latest/): building a service on SQL databases with the crate, the inbox and the outbox
- [Getting started](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-sqlx/latest/guides/getting-started/): the features, a queue table, a first handler and its test on SQLite with no server
- [Enqueueing jobs](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-sqlx/latest/guides/enqueueing/): a task written in the transaction of the data it serves, later, or by priority
- [Retries and dead letters](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-sqlx/latest/guides/retries/): a retry now or later, a backoff the handler computes, the attempt cap and the dead letter
- [Long jobs and the claim form](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-sqlx/latest/guides/claim-forms/): the row lock, the lease and the advisory lock, and what each does after a crash
- [Ordering](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-sqlx/latest/guides/ordering/): FIFO groups and partition keys
- [Transactional handlers](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-sqlx/latest/guides/transactional/): a handler that writes through its delivery's transaction, committed with the acknowledgement
- [Several instances](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-sqlx/latest/guides/scaling/): several processes on one table, workers, the pool they need, and waking on a publish
- [Relaying to another broker](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-sqlx/latest/guides/relay/): an event row committed with the business data, and an inbox handler that publishes it to another RustStream broker
- [The outbox](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-sqlx/latest/guides/outbox/): tracking what a service publishes until a consumer has processed it
- [Testing](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-sqlx/latest/guides/testing/): `TestApp::start` on the production app over a real database, with a paused clock
- [Running in production](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-sqlx/latest/guides/production/): the schema, the pool and the database server

## Components

- [Components](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-sqlx/latest/components/): the parts of the crate a service uses, one page each
- [SqlxBroker](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-sqlx/latest/components/broker/): the broker over the service's pool, its connections, startup, shutdown, prelude and errors
- [Inbox](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-sqlx/latest/components/tables/): `#[derive(Inbox)]`, the column roles, `InboxSpec` by hand, the insert, events of the service's own and the checked mode
- [Payload](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-sqlx/latest/components/messages/): payload mode, row mode, and a row that does not decode
- [Headers](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-sqlx/latest/components/headers/): a headers column, `HeaderColumn`, the headers layout with `InboxHeaders`, `HeaderField` and a fetch over a join
- [InboxQueue](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-sqlx/latest/components/subscriptions/): a subscription to one queue: the poll interval, workers, batches, FIFO groups, dedicated threads and subscriptions by name
- [Forms](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-sqlx/latest/components/forms/): the row lock, the lease and the advisory lock forms, and a lock of the service's own
- [Outcomes](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-sqlx/latest/components/settlement/): what each handler outcome does to a row, `retry_after` and the dead letter
- [Transactional](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-sqlx/latest/components/transactions/): `.transactional()` and `Ctx<keys::Tx<DB>>`, and the isolation level or SQLite mode
- [Context](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-sqlx/latest/components/context/): `Ctx<keys::..>`: the transaction, the pool and the attempt
- [Time](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-sqlx/latest/components/time/): "now" from the host, the database or a clock of the service's own, and the time types
- [Repository](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-sqlx/latest/components/publishing/): a publish written into a table through the service's own `Publish`, and routes
- [Wake](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-sqlx/latest/components/wake/): a publish that wakes its subscriptions, and `LISTEN/NOTIFY` on Postgres
- [Databases](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-sqlx/latest/components/databases/): Postgres, MySQL and MariaDB, SQLite, an `AnyPool`, and a dialect of the service's own
- [AsyncAPI](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-sqlx/latest/components/asyncapi/): the server and the channels the generated document names, behind the `asyncapi` feature
- [Testing](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-sqlx/latest/components/testing/): `TestApp::start` over a real database behind the `testing` feature, and the same body live
- [Transactional outbox](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-sqlx/latest/components/outbox/): the record, the registry, the middlewares, the republish, `wrap`, the pool and the test switch

## Architecture

- [Architecture](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-sqlx/latest/architecture/): how a queue in a SQL table works, where the crate sits between the database and the RustStream runtime, and what that costs
- [Tables](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-sqlx/latest/architecture/queues/): a row is a message, a group is a queue, and the columns' roles decide when a row is due
- [Claims](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-sqlx/latest/architecture/queues/claims/): the row lock, the lease and the advisory lock, each priced in connections
- [Transactions](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-sqlx/latest/architecture/queues/transactions/): the transactions the crate opens for a delivery, and the one a transactional handler writes through
- [Waking](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-sqlx/latest/architecture/queues/waking/): the poll interval, and a publish or a notification that cuts it short
- [Outbox](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-sqlx/latest/architecture/outbox/): the record of each publish, its mark on acknowledgement, and the republish at startup
- [Design](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-sqlx/latest/architecture/design/): between the RustStream runtime and the service's pool, with SQL built once per subscription
- [Lifecycle](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-sqlx/latest/architecture/lifecycle/): `new`, `connect`, the statements prepared at startup, and `shutdown`
- [Path](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-sqlx/latest/architecture/path/): one row from the claim through the handler and the reply to its settlement
- [Settlement](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-sqlx/latest/architecture/settlement/): what each outcome writes into a queue table in each claim form
- [Lanes](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-sqlx/latest/architecture/lanes/): a claim in flight per free worker within the pool, and `workers_by_key(n)` lanes
- [Benchmarks](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-sqlx/latest/architecture/benchmarks/): throughput against a raw sqlx loop, the outbox's cost to an app, and the instructions and allocations of the crate's code
- [Benchmarks: Numbers](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-sqlx/latest/architecture/benchmarks/numbers/): what each published number measures, and what it does not allow you to conclude
- [Benchmarks: Methodology](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-sqlx/latest/architecture/benchmarks/methodology/): the three loops, the run on a real database, the throughput grid and the code count
